dedupe_keys.name: inventory of school buildings in central sulawesi indonesia

description: This dataset is an inventory of 2,536 school buildings in Central Sulawesi, Indonesia, the region struck by the magnitude 7.5 Palu earthquake of 28 September 2018, which triggered liquefaction, a tsunami and landslides and damaged or destroyed at least 1,299 schools. It was developed by Eyitayo Opabola, Carmine Galasso and Tiziana Rossetto of University College London with IUSS Pavia, Tadulako University and the Tsunami and Disaster Mitigation Research Center of Syiah Kuala University, combining sidewalk and remote surveys to show a cheaper way of building regional inventories in low- and middle-income countries. For each building it records location, number of storeys, use and occupant numbers, age, lateral load resisting system, materials, structural vulnerabilities and condition after the 2018 earthquake. Access: open download from Zenodo of the school database, rapid visual survey forms and principal interviews, with a readme. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: a one-off 2022 survey of one region; remote-survey attributes are less certain than field ones. Simulation uses are seismic and multi-hazard risk assessment of schools, prioritising retrofit, and post-event damage and recovery analysis. Related records: other building inventories for exposure models.
